newsitem.title: CANADA: Polls show Canada's Conservatives gaining ground.
newsitem.headline: Polls show Canada's Conservatives gaining ground.

text.p: A poll released on Saturday showed Canada's Conservative party gaining strength in the national election campaign and making big strides in French-speaking Quebec at the expense of the province's separatist party.

The poll, conducted by Environics and published in the Toronto Globe and Mail newspaper, indicated similar results as three others released on Friday showing Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberal party hanging onto a big majority of decided voters nationally in the runup to the June 2 election.
Support for the Liberals, however, slipped since early this week when Conservative leader Jean Charest made a strong showing in two nationally televised leaders debates.

The Environics-Globe and Mail poll, conducted May 13-15, showed the Liberals with 40 percent of decided voters, Conservatives with 25 percent, Reform with 18 percent, the Bloc Quebecois with seven percent and the New Democratic Party with nine percent.

The results showed a nine percentage point gain for the Conservatives, seven percent drop for the Liberals and five percent drop for the Bloc from the last Environics poll conducted March 11-31, before the election was called.
However, it also showed late-campaign volatility with 49 percent of those surveyed saying they might change their vote before election day.
The poll surveyed 1,912 voters from all 10 provinces and had a margin of error of plus or minus 2.3 percent 19 times out of 20.
In Quebec, the Conservatives had 36 percent support among decided voters, a dramatic jump from 10 percent in the last survey, the Environics poll said.

The Conservative gain appeared to be at the expense of the Bloc, whose 44 percent support in March plunged to 27 percent in the latest poll that followed the Monday and Tuesday debates. Charest was considered the winner by a majority of voters in numerous surveys.
The Quebec results differed from those in a Reuters-Zogby International poll relased on Friday showing the Bloc six percentage points ahead of the Conservatives, but 12 points behind the Liberals.
A computer projection of the Environics poll showed a big shift in the makeup of Canada's 301-seat parliament after the June election, the Globe and Mail reported.
It projected the Liberals would keep their majority by winning 186 seats, the Conservatives would gain official opposition status with 50, the right-wing Reform party would win 47 and the Bloc 17.
The Bloc became official opposition after the 1993 election by taking 54 seats.

Like the Environics-Globe and Mail and Reuters/Zogby polls, others conducted by Gallup Canada Inc. and Strategic Council, results of which were released on Friday, showed the governing Liberals still well ahead in the campaign with the Conservatives gaining the most ground.
